stage1.impression: A warm, plausibly proportioned timber room with a well-dressed back bar, but it reads as CG at once: the three guests are featureless smoothed mannequins rather than motion-blurred people, the clerestory band is a flat orange strip of thin fluted plastic with moire and a few fireflies (signage, not premium acrylic), and the oak baffle and porch read as smooth veneer doors with no slots. The grade pushes every surface, plaster and concrete included, to one orange, and no EARF speaker or saturated product colour is visible. A magazine would see a generic hotel-lounge render, not a specific, well-made place.

blocking_9: Guests must read as real people in motion (clothing, hands, hair, a glass), not smooth grey mannequins; or remove them and leave signs of life instead (coat on a stool, a record out of its sleeve, half-full glasses)
The acrylic band must read as thick cast fins with glowing polished edges and depth, not a flat emissive orange strip with moire
The grade must keep plaster, terrazzo and quartzite near-neutral warm-grey so oak and the amber band are the only strong warm notes (plaster r/b ratio under 2.2 instead of 3.0)
The lantern's slotted baffle must read as slotted (shadowed slot lines from a raking graze), and the porch as a solid oak volume, not veneer cupboard doors
An EARF product with its tint must be legible as the colour hero somewhere in frame
Floor and right-hand banquette must hold texture (terrazzo chips, leather sheen) instead of falling to lum 15

defects.what: Bartender/guest figure is a smooth faceless mannequin with blob head and tube limbs; reads as a game placeholder
Seated figure on the right is the same mannequin model; repeated asset
Acrylic band: flat saturated orange, fine flutes alias into moire, no edge glow or depth, two white firefly specks near x 680 y 130 and x 760 y 160
Baffle and porch read as smooth veneer doors; grain is stretched vertical streaks, no slots, no joinery shadow
Black steel head trim reads as a flat black stripe with no sheen or edge
Right plaster wall is a featureless dark brown field (median 13.9), no lime texture, no light pool
Foreground tables and banquette crushed to median 15, tables read as flat black slabs
Terrazzo floor reads as noisy speckle, not honed stone with sheen; no reflection of the band or pendants
Ceiling a dead dark field with one bare downlight spot; no fixture detail
Pendant shade is a near-white blown bowl that reads as a CG primitive
Global orange cast: every material shares one hue (oak r73 g40 b21); plaster, quartzite, steel lose identity

changes.problem: The people are smooth mannequins that announce CG more than anything else in frame.

evidence.measured: Crop at 3x: blob head, tube arms, uniform grey-brown shading, no clothing folds or hands; second identical figure at [830, 440, 970, 600].

change.to: replace with dressed scanned human assets (different body, clothing and hair per figure), shutter 0.4 so the blur trails a hand or head only; or set people to 0 and dress signs of life instead (coat over a stool, two half-full glasses with ice, a record leaning out of its sleeve on the counter)

changes.expected: Figures read as people turning or reaching, with cloth, skin and hair; the frame reads as a lived night rather than a showroom with placeholders.

changes.problem: The grade turns every surface the same orange, so plaster, quartzite and terrazzo lose their identity and the frame looks monochrome rather than warm.
changes.expected: Plaster and quartzite sit warm-grey, oak keeps its honey tone, the amber band becomes the most saturated warm note.

changes.problem: The acrylic band reads as a flat orange lightbox with fluted moire, not thick cast fins with glowing edges.

evidence.measured: lum_median 108.6, lum_range 152 but driven by alias moire; delta-E 9.6 to amber #C8782A; no brighter fin edges visible at 2x.

change.to: 0.04, plus edge-lit grazes along the fin tops (thin emitter strip above the fins, 2400 K) so the polished fin edges carry the light; render at full 2400 x 1600 so the fin pitch resolves without moire

changes.expected: A darker amber field with bright fin edges and visible depth between fins; reads as thick cast acrylic.

changes.problem: The baffle and porch read as smooth veneer cupboard doors; the slots and the porch's volume do not show.

evidence.measured: falloff top to bottom 127 -> 31 in 8 bins, lum_range only 68; no slot shadow lines visible at 2x.

change.to: a linear raking graze from the floor line at the baffle foot (foot line 9.0 -> 14.0) and a narrow top graze at 0.6 W/m2 so each slot casts a shadow; add a 2700 K spot 20 W, 20 deg on the porch's face from the side

changes.expected: Slots read as dark lines at regular pitch, the porch's returns separate from the baffle, light rises from the floor and falls from the top in a pool rather than one gradient.

changes.problem: The right half of the frame (plaster wall, banquette, tables) is a dead dark field with no pools of light.

change.to: 4 x spot 40.0 W, 24 deg aimed at the table tops, plus a small table lamp (EARF Core in its tint) on the nearest table

changes.expected: Pools of light on each table top with glasses catching highlights; the banquette's leather shows sheen; dark between pools.

changes.problem: No EARF product or saturated tint is visible, so the frame has no colour hero and reads as a generic bar.

evidence.measured: All regions share one hue (r:g:b about 3.5:2:1); no saturated non-orange patch anywhere.

change.to: shift the camera so a tinted Core or Hemisphere lamp on the counter or back bar sits on the left third in the foreground, keeping the lantern's face centred; 35 mm

changes.expected: One tinted EARF object reads at a glance as the only saturated colour, establishing the brand and a specific place.

changes.problem: The terrazzo floor reads as noisy speckle without the sheen of honed stone, and the counter top has no reflection of the pendants.

evidence.measured: lum_median 29.7, p5 2.5, crush 6.1%; no specular streak under the band or pendant at 1:1.

change.to: honed roughness about 0.25 with larger chips (8-15 mm) and a warm-grey ground, so the band and downlights lay soft streaks on the floor

changes.expected: Floor shows a soft reflection of the amber band and reads as stone at scale.

changes.problem: The pendant shade is a blown white primitive and the ceiling is empty, both reading as CG.

evidence.measured: ceiling lum_median 10.4, range 15.6; pendant bowl near-white at [150,265,195,300].

change.to: haze 0.012/m so the downlight cones and band show faint volume; dim the pendant's inner surface and give its shade a metal or glass material with an edge highlight

changes.expected: Soft cones under each downlight and a faint glow below the band; ceiling holds shape without being lit.

out_of_scope.request: Show the Tropos pair in Ember (open the porch or glaze the lantern's face so the speakers read inside)
out_of_scope.why: The architecture is fixed and the pair is placed inside the closed lantern; only the owner can decide to show it from this view.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the plain door-like porch leaves with visibly slotted or framed joinery
out_of_scope.why: The porch and baffle design is fixed; only the lighting can bring out what is drawn.
